primitives.name: NHL Performance Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: NHL Performance Model Goal: Given that a player was drafted into the NHL, model his value to his NHL team based on his amateur statistics.
primitives.assumptions: Amateur performance scales linearly with professional contribution; PTPP normalizes for team strength.

The core operators define a dual modeling system: one for predicting draft eligibility (probabilistic), another for estimating post-draft performance (regression-based). The draft probability model leverages logistic regression to map player traits to a binary outcome, while the NHL performance model applies a derived kernel—PTPP—to quantify value. Both rely on scaled statistics to mitigate variance from differing sample sizes. The failure mode occurs when data is sparse or biased, particularly in early-season leagues. Temporal shifts due to the pandemic introduce heterogeneity in data availability, which the model attempts to correct through league-specific scaling. The PTPP metric isolates individual performance from team context, enabling cross-league comparisons. This duality enables GSI to compute both selection likelihood and expected contribution, while GSE simulates evolving player states under varying data regimes.
